newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Shareholders agree to liquidate Venezuela's Viasa.
newsitem.headline: Shareholders agree to liquidate Venezuela's Viasa.

text.p: Shareholders of Venezuelan international carrier Visas agreed Thursday to liquidate the airline within a year, according to a statement read out after a shareholders meeting.

"The shareholders proposed to instruct the company's administration to ask for the competent court's permission to move toward ... the amicable liquidation of its business within a period not exceeding 12 months," William Bracho, workers' representative on Viasa's board of directors, said.
Viasa, which is 45-percent-owned by Spanish airline Iberia, has been grounded since Jan. 23 when workers rejcted a rescue plan that involved job cuts and route reductions.
The airline, in which the state privatization body Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) owns 40 percent, has debts totaling more than $150 million.

The FIV said in a statement the decision to liquidate Viasa was inevitable "although since the start of talks (the FIV) has always been oriented toward seeking the best alternatives to save the company."

Iberia and the FIV hammered out another rescue plan in Madrid last month but officials had said in recent days that the company's debts were too large and they were not prepared to inject more money to save it.
Viasa has not made a profit since it was semi-privatized in 1991.
The shareholders agreed to set up a trust fund with $20 million to meet the severance payments of Viasa's 2,250 employees.
Venezuela's leading bank Banco Provincial owns the remaining 15 percent of Viasa.
